title: Decentralized capacity-aware geo harmonization for latency SLO continuity
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Implement a decentralized, capacity-aware geo harmonization policy so that requests maintain latency SLOs during regional perturbations while minimizing cross-region traffic and preserving sticky pinning where possible. The policy must combine latency-based routing, geo pinning affinity, and a continuous capacity score to drive steering decisions. It should support graceful degradation (tiered shedding), per-customer affinity bounds, and circuit-breaker gates that open based on SLO breach signals and capacity signals.

Constraints: must be implementable in the existing request director (golang service), compatible with existing model variant fallback graph, and operate with eventual consistency between region controllers (no global master). Observability hooks required for token-level cost and latency attribution. Rollout must be canaryed across low-traffic customers before enabling account-wide.

Acceptance criteria: (1) On synthetic regional degradation the platform keeps P95 latency below configured SLO+10% for 90% of traffic after failover behavior, (2) cross-region egress increase is limited to configured budget per account, (3) automated shedding triggers to preserve cluster health when capacity_score < threshold, (4) dashboards show expected signals and circuit-breaker state transitions, (5) full automated rollback if error rate > 1% for canary cohort.
proposal:
We propose a hybrid steering algorithm: each region computes a normalized capacity_score and a rolling latency_score for each model variant, both in the range [0,1]. Score aggregation: final_region_score = alpha * latency_score + (1 - alpha) * capacity_score, alpha configurable per-route (default 0.7). Geo pinning is implemented as soft affinity: if userpin_score > pin_threshold, prefer home region unless final_region_score falls below a hysteresis-adjusted failover floor. Circuit breaker gates evaluate three signals: sustained SLO breach (p95 > limit for T minutes), capacity_score below critical, and backlog queue growth rate. When any two signals are active, the gate opens and traffic is steered to next-best region respecting per-account egress caps. Load shedding is tiered: first reduce max_tokens for best-effort traffic, then reject non-essential routes, then hard reject when host protection is required. All decisions are local with periodic peer heartbeats to exchange summarized capacity_snapshot (10s granularity).

Key novel elements: decentralized harmonization (no single global allocator), soft geo affinity with hysteresis to avoid flapping, continuous capacity_score (rather than binary up/down), tiered shedding knobs tied to request class and SLAs.
design_decisions: Keep steering decision local to region director to avoid single point of failure and reduce control plane latency
Use continuous capacity_score computed from free_gpus, load_fraction, and pending_queue_weight instead of binary thresholds
Default alpha=0.7 to prioritize latency but allow operator override per route for cost-sensitive customers
Soft geo pinning with two hysteresis windows: failover_window (short-term) and stickiness_window (long-term) to balance stability vs locality
Circuit breaker requires at least two concurrent signals to open (reduces false positives from noisy metrics)
Expose shedding knobs via per-customer policy with global safe caps to prevent unlimited cross-region egress
implementation_plan: ENG: add capacity_score computation in region-metrics pipeline (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/dir-serv/PR-4821)
ENG: implement local steering module that consumes latency_score + capacity_score (branch: feat/geo-harmonize)
ENG: add soft-pin metadata to account config (DB migration script: github.com/redwood-inference/account-service/PR-2134)
ENG: circuit-breaker state machine and persistent window store (use existing ring buffer in director-state)
DEVOPS: extend heartbeat sidecar to publish summarized capacity_snapshot to peers (helm chart update in charts/dir)
QA: create integration harness for multi-region chaos tests (see testing plan)
rollout_plan: Step 0: Feature flag behind 'geo_harmonize_v2' with default off for all customers
Step 1: Internal-only canary (20% of internal traffic) for 48h monitor metrics and manual rollback criteria
Step 2: Low-risk customers opt-in (beta flag) for 7 days; automated rollback trigger if canary SLOs degrade
Step 3: Ramp to 10% production traffic across a geographically diverse slice over 3 days, observe capacity/egress metrics
Step 4: Full enable for customers with permissive egress policies; gradually expand to all after 4-week observation
Rollback conditions: increase in 1-minute error rate > 1% above baseline, sustained p95 > SLO+20% for 30 minutes, or >2 regions reporting critical capacity simultaneously
testing_and_simulation: Unit tests for capacity_score math and hysteresis logic
E2E simulation harness: synthetic clients with region affinity, inject latency tails and node OOM events
Chaos tests: kill inference worker GPU pods in a region and verify steering and shedding behavior
Load tests: run production-like traffic at 1.5x QPS to validate shedding thresholds and cost cap enforcement
Backpressure simulation: synthetic backlog growth to validate circuit-breaker gating and state transitions
metrics_and_alerting: Per-region final_region_score (timeseries) - low values indicate steer-away candidates
P95 latency per-route per-region (SLO) with rolling window alarms
Cross-region egress by account (7-day rolling) and per-deploy budget alerts
Circuit-breaker open rate and average open duration per-region
Shedding action count by type (token_reduction, route_reject, hard_reject)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: oscillation between regions causing increased latency and cost. Mitigation: hysteresis windows and rate-limited peer updates.
Risk: cross-region egress spikes for customers. Mitigation: per-account egress budgets and soft rejection before cross-region steering escalates.
Risk: incorrect capacity_score tuning leads to over-shedding. Mitigation: start with conservative critical thresholds and use blue/green for tuning.
Risk: observability blind spots during rollouts. Mitigation: extended retention for canary cohorts and synthetic transactions for critical paths.
